gbm_population_evidence.quote: At least 18 years of age on the day of signing informed consent, with histologically confirmed diagnosis of GBM or astrocytoma Grade 4\^.
Histological confirmation using the 2016 or 2021 World Health Organization (WHO) Classification of Tumours of the central nervous system (CNS) is acceptable and classification edition will be noted.

candidate_evidence.quote: A humanised immunoglobulin G4 (IgG4) monoclonal antibody (mAb) specific for the programmed cell death 1 (PD-1) receptor
The goal of this clinical trial is to test a combined therapy approach (allogeneic cytomegalovirus \[CMV\]-specific T cells and pembrolizumab) in patients with brain cancer.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: T Cells and Pembrolizumab for Recurrent and Newly Diagnosed Glioblastoma
Part 2 Group B: Patients with newly diagnosed disease.

role_evidence.quote: Pembrolizumab infusions will commence seven days (±3 days) after the final T-cell infusion, and be administered every 6 weeks (Q6W).
A humanised immunoglobulin G4 (IgG4) monoclonal antibody (mAb) specific for the programmed cell death 1 (PD-1) receptor
Allogeneic cytomegalovirus (CMV)-specific T cells generated from the blood of healthy CMV-seropositive donors

coder_notes: Pembrolizumab is the only pharmacological investigational agent alongside a cell therapy, so experimental_monotherapy per worked example. Brief summary mentions T cells as monotherapy as well, but all registered arms list both interventions. 'GBM or astrocytoma Grade 4' with WHO 2016 or 2021 acceptable and no IDH requirement -> historical; under WHO 2021 'astrocytoma grade 4' may include IDH-mutant tumours. Newly diagnosed patients delay standard adjuvant temozolomide; temozolomide is permitted but not a registered intervention and not stated as given to every patient, so not listed. CMV serology and HLA matching are not tumour biomarkers.
